paragraphs: The Pastor, writing to my good friend Gaius: Bro, I genuinely love you! We're the best of friends, and I'm praying that everything in your life goes well—your health, your daily stuff, and especially your soul! I was SO happy when some friends showed up and told me you're still walking in the Truth. Honestly, nothing makes me happier than hearing that my spiritual kids are staying on the right path!

Dear friend, when you open your home to other Christians—even total strangers—you're making faith real and visible. They came back and told the whole church about your love. That's amazing work you're doing, helping these travelers along their journey. It's the kind of hospitality that honors God himself! These people went out representing Jesus and they don't take money from non-believers. So we should absolutely support them. When we give them a place to stay and food to eat, we become partners in spreading the Truth.

I actually wrote something like this to the church earlier, but Diotrephes—this guy who loves being the boss of everything—totally dismissed what I said. If I come visit, trust me, I'm going to call him out for all the trash he's been talking about us.

And it gets worse. He not only refuses to welcome traveling Christians himself, but he actually tries to stop OTHER people from helping them too. And if anyone does welcome them? He kicks them out of the church. Wild.
Friend, don't follow that kind of evil behavior. Follow the good instead. The person who does good is doing God's work. The person who does evil has clearly never understood God at all.
Everyone has great things to say about Demetrius—and the Truth itself backs him up! We agree completely, and you know we don't just hand out endorsements to anyone.
I have SO much more to tell you, but I'd rather not do it through a letter. I'm hoping to see you face-to-face soon so we can have a real heart-to-heart conversation.
Peace to you! All our friends here say hi. Give my love to each of our friends there.
